title: A Zero Knowledge Proof framework for Cardano based on Hydra and ZK-SNARKS

ms.promise:
Context: The general objective of this project is the integration of existing open source tooling, such as CIRCOM and SNARKJS, with the Cardano ecosystem. The two elliptic curves compatible with SNARKJS are BN128 AND BLS12-381. We need to study both curves to determine which better adapts with Hydra, as well as other tooling alternatives.
Outputs:
・Study of the elliptic curve BN128, including a mathematical analysis of the "tower of field extensions" associated.
・Study of the elliptic curve BLS12-381.
・Analysis of the current ecosystem of ZK open source toolings.
・Study of the viability of ZK tooling to generate ZK proof verifications using smart contracts in Cardano.
ms.criteria: Submitted documentation contains a comprehensive description of results of the promised studies and analysis.
ms.report:
Context: The general objective of this project is the integration of existing open source tooling, such as CIRCOM and SNARKJS, with the Cardano ecosystem, in order to construct ZK proofs. The two elliptic curves compatible with SNARKJS are BN128 AND BLS12-381. We need to study both curves to determine which better adapts with Hydra, as well as other tooling alternatives.
Promised Outputs for Milestone 1:
・Study of the elliptic curve BN128, including a mathematical analysis of the "tower of field extensions" associated.
・Study of the elliptic curve BLS12-381.
・Analysis of the current ecosystem of ZK open source toolings.
・Study of the viability of ZK tooling to generate ZK proof verifications using smart contracts in Cardano.

Relevant to all the promised outputs, we completed a Technical Report which can be found in https://github.com/Modulo-P/groth-pairing/blob/main/technical_specifications.pdf .
Output 1
Completed a mathematical study, including the proof of two relevant theorems, of the tower of field extensions needed to implement a “Weils pairing” compatible with elliptic curve BN128. The study also outlines how the field extensions are to be implemented in Haskell. This study is documented in chapter 4 of https://github.com/Modulo-P/groth-pairing/blob/main/technical_specifications.pdf .
Based on this mathematical study, as well as our previous experience with Miller’s algorithm (see https://github.com/Modulo-P/miller-first-study), we implemented in Haskell a Weils pairing compatible with elliptic curve BN128. Our repository https://github.com/Modulo-P/groth-pairing contains this implementation.
Performed property based testing using the standard Haskell library QuickCheck to ensure that our pairing implementation satisfies the crucial bilinearity property; see https://github.com/Modulo-P/groth-pairing/tree/main/logs .
Output 2
In the same mathematical study mentioned in Output 1 we included a section covering the few modifications needed for elliptic curve BLS

ms.promise:
Context: The Groth16 protocol for the execution of ZKPs consists of three parts, of which the first two are executed offchain. The third one, namely "the ZK proof verification", is ideally executed onchain. The main part of the verification algorithm is the so called "Weil's pairing".
Outputs:
・Unit tests for either the BN128 or BLS12-381 elliptic curve, as well as the elementary curve BLS6_6, confirming that the necessary properties (such as "bilineality" of the Weil's Paring) necessary for implementing the Groth16 protocol are satisfied.
・Will implement the onchain code using at least two languages:
・PlutusTx (Haskell)
・Aiken
・Optionally, a combination of PlutusTx and Plutarch (Haskell)
・Optimization analysis (for all the languages used) of either elliptic curve, in terms of compilation to UPLC.
・Performance tests and comparisons.
ms.criteria:
Provided repository contains:
・The onchain code ZK-proof verification code written in (at least) both Plutus (Haskell) and Aiken.
・Has reproducible unit tests confirming the desired properties of the Weil's pairing.
・Has submitted comparative performance tests.

ms.promise:
Context: Given that the ZKP verification algorithm requires more resources than those provided by nodes on Cardano's mainnet, this project will use Hydra heads to implement onchain ZK verification (of ZK proofs generated offchain). For the solution to be valuable to the community, user documentation needs to be provided.
Outputs: 
・Configuration and deployment of Hydra nodes for the execution of the smart contracts with the ZK algorithms.
・Creation of scripts for the offchain generation of ZK proofs with the open source tooling chosen in Milestone 1.
・Design of the workflow for the interaction between the Web3 offchain code (generating the ZK proofs) and the smart contracts running on Hydra (implementing the onchain ACCEPT/REJECT verification of the ZK proofs).
・Design of the Web3 infrastructure for interaction with Hydra and the smart contracts.
・Documentation and use cases
・Assemble technical documentation. We will evaluate the usage of an instance of the "Andamio project" to make this documentation more accesible.
・Assemble use cases and ZK examples. This includes a refinement of the "Mastermind" game as a successful use case.
ms.criteria: The final solution successfully integrates the smart contracts written in Haskll/Aiken with Hydra and a Web3 interface for a complete implementation of the Groth16 protocol of ZK-SNARKS, enabling an hypothetical user to deploy a ZKP solution for some use case. User documentation has been provided.
